open_obligations: Check that 'approximate global equilibrium' in Buhl et al. matches A-leading Stackelberg equilibria.
Check that the safety case accounts for the stability and A-provability conditions.
Note the guarantee is average-case over inputs.
out.other_title: Theorem 6.2: correct answers at A-leading Stackelberg equilibria (prob. 1 - 5 eps)
out.rationale: Buhl et al.'s key claim 2 is that in approximate global equilibria the system errs on at most an eps'-fraction of cases, with prover-estimator debate as the example protocol. Brown-Cohen et al.'s Theorem 6.2 gives correct answers with probability at least 1 - 5 eps at alpha-approximate A-leading Stackelberg equilibria, given rho-stability and A-provability, which is the kind of result claim 2 needs.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the safety case's claim that approximate equilibria of the debate game imply a bounded error rate

text: The authors list four key claims a developer must defend: (1) training has reached an approximate global equilibrium of the debate game; (2) in approximate global equilibria the system makes mistakes in at most an eps'-fraction of cases; (3) during deployment, with online training, the error rate will not drift past eps; and (4) the system cannot cause unacceptable outcomes given an error rate of eps.
title: Four key claims of the debate safety case: equilibrium, error bound, no drift, low stakes
